significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish both a phenomenon and a mechanism: facts with "the least overlapping circuits" are less behaviorally consistent across query formats because a "shared mid-layer storage locus" feeds format-specific access heads whose ablation selectively breaks one format. This is a form-(iii) predictive coupling between circuit overlap and behavioral consistency, strengthened by a causal decomposition of storage versus access; it fixes expectations for unseen fact-format pairs and changes whether prompt-consistency scores such as those studied by Jiang et al. (2020) and Elazar et al. (2021) should be interpreted as evidence about knowledge storage or retrieval. Verified false—especially if the same components mediate every format or storage loci also vary—would rule out the stated access-pathway explanation; the overlap and selective-ablation assertions make true and false distinguishable despite some ambiguity in "partially distinct." Topic substitution would leave only the generic question of query-dependent retrieval, which would not merit this score; the specific shared-storage/access decomposition and overlap-consistency law are what raise it above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "circuit-overlap (Jaccard)" score over causally implicated components, interpreted as a predictor of "behavioral consistency," together with format-specific ablation targets. It is mainly post hoc because extracting circuits generally requires running and analyzing the relevant fact-format cases, although the asserted overlap-consistency relation could predict which additional phrasings will fail once overlap is measured. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive claim still predicts lower consistency for lower overlap, so more than a lookup procedure transfers; however, the hypothesis covers a class of query formats and facts without explicitly asserting robustness across architectures, scales, or training regimes, and its concrete uptake is chiefly by interpretability and factual-consistency researchers rather than deployers. Topic substitution would provide neither this metric nor its predicted relation, so the score comes from the claim-specific transferable handle rather than the broad importance of factual retrieval.
